---
title: "Fitting number of claims - Poisson vs Negative Binomial"
---


```{r}
# ============================================================
# Method of Moments Estimation
# Claim count data
# ============================================================

# Sample moments
mean_sample <- 0.1264
var_sample  <- 0.1628

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Poisson distribution
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# For X ~ Poisson(lambda):
#
# E[X] = lambda
# Var(X) = lambda
#
# Method of Moments:
lambda_hat <- mean_sample

cat("Poisson distribution\n")
cat("lambda =", lambda_hat, "\n\n")


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Negative Binomial Type 2
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# X = number of failures before the k-th success
#
# E[X]   = kq / p
# Var(X) = kq / p^2
#
# where q = 1 - p.
#
# Method of Moments:
#
# From
#     Var(X) / E[X] = 1 / p
#
# therefore
#     p = E[X] / Var(X)
#
# and
#     k = E[X]^2 / (Var(X) - E[X])

p_hat <- mean_sample / var_sample
q_hat <- 1 - p_hat

k_hat <- mean_sample^2 / (var_sample - mean_sample)

cat("Negative Binomial Type 2\n")
cat("k =", k_hat, "\n")
cat("p =", p_hat, "\n")
cat("q =", q_hat, "\n\n")


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Check the fitted theoretical moments
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Poisson
poisson_mean <- lambda_hat
poisson_var  <- lambda_hat


# Negative Binomial Type 2
nb_mean <- k_hat * q_hat / p_hat
nb_var  <- k_hat * q_hat / p_hat^2

results <- data.frame(
  Distribution = c(
    "Poisson",
    "Negative Binomial Type 2"
  ),
  Mean = c(
    poisson_mean,
    nb_mean
  ),
  Variance = c(
    poisson_var,
    nb_var
  )
)

results
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Expected number of policies by number of claims
# ------------------------------------------------------------

n <- 10000

# Claim-count categories
claim_categories <- c("0", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5+")


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Poisson expected numbers
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Probabilities for 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4 claims
poisson_prob <- dpois(0:4, lambda = lambda_hat)

# Probability of 5 or more claims
poisson_prob_5plus <- ppois(
  4,
  lambda = lambda_hat,
  lower.tail = FALSE
)

# Combine probabilities
poisson_prob <- c(poisson_prob, poisson_prob_5plus)

# Convert probabilities to expected numbers of policies
poisson_expected <- n * poisson_prob


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Negative Binomial expected numbers
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Probabilities for 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4 claims
nb_prob <- dnbinom(
  0:4,
  size = k_hat,
  prob = p_hat
)

# Probability of 5 or more claims
nb_prob_5plus <- pnbinom(
  4,
  size = k_hat,
  prob = p_hat,
  lower.tail = FALSE
)

# Combine probabilities
nb_prob <- c(nb_prob, nb_prob_5plus)

# Convert probabilities to expected numbers of policies
nb_expected <- n * nb_prob


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Create comparison table
# ------------------------------------------------------------

expected_policies <- data.frame(
  Claims = claim_categories,
  Observed = c(8959, 852, 160, 24, 5, 0),
  Poisson = poisson_expected,
  Negative_Binomial = nb_expected
)

expected_policies
```



```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Comparison of fitted probabilities and expected frequencies
# ------------------------------------------------------------

expected_policies <- data.frame(
  Claims = claim_categories,
  
  Observed = c(8959, 852, 160, 24, 5, 0),
  
  Poisson_Probability = poisson_prob,
  Poisson_Expected = poisson_expected,
  
  NB_Probability = nb_prob,
  NB_Expected = nb_expected
)

expected_policies
```



```{r}
expected_policies <- data.frame(
  Claims = claim_categories,
  Observed = c(8959, 852, 160, 24, 5, 0),
  Poisson = poisson_expected,
  Negative_Binomial = nb_expected
)

expected_policies$Poisson <- round(expected_policies$Poisson, 1)
expected_policies$Negative_Binomial <- round(expected_policies$Negative_Binomial, 1)

expected_policies
```
